texts: good. Bevin Coombe is recorded as a named individual who is a member of the keeper class, with nothing added and nothing dropped. One thing to know: capitalized "Keeper" is read as the ordinary common noun "one who keeps", so the parse also carries the definitional atom that a keeper can keep; that is harmless here, but it is the reading the bare sentence licenses rather than an office/title reading.
Thirty lanterns stand in the Northcove.

good. the thirty lanterns become one counted group of thirty placed in the Northcove, plus a fireable rule that puts each individual lantern there too, so both "how many lanterns?" and "is this lantern in the Northcove?" resolve. "Stand in" is correctly recorded as a static position rather than an event, which is what the sentence means. Northcove is kept as a name with no separate "cove" type atom, which is the right conservative reading — the sentence never states what kind of place it is.
